the 22 S particles and their protein components are present in a broad range of cells, including oocytes, somatic cells and erythrocytes of amphibians, and that the particles are present in the cytoplams as well as in nuclei.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the particles are present in the cytoplams of a variety of cell types, including oocytes, and are not confined to the nucleus as was previously thought.

the Xenopus 22 S particle, which is a major component of the oocyte nucleoplasm, is a ubiquitous cytoplasmic and nuclear protein constituent of transcriptionally active cells of a broad range, including oocytes, somatic cells, embryonic and cancer cells, but not of mature erythrocyte, spermatozoa and spermatids.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are many different types of particles in the cytoplams of cells and that they are involved in a variety of cellular functions.
